evals.name: read-filter-sort
evals.prompt: Using our PocketBase, list every active challenge in the 'mcpskill_read' collection (active = true), sorted by points from highest to lowest. Give me each title with its points.
evals.expected_output: Discovers schema, then find_records with filter_template="active = {:a}" / filter_params={"a": true} and sort="-points". Reports exactly: Buffer Overflow 500, Crypto Basics 300, XSS Warmup 150, SQL Injection 101 100. Excludes the two inactive rows. No writes.
assertions: Calls describe_schema or describe_collection for mcpskill_read before querying
Uses filter_template with a {:placeholder} plus filter_params, not a hand-built filter string with literal values
Passes a descending sort on points (sort="-points") rather than sorting in prose after the fact
Final answer lists exactly the 4 active rows and omits 'Reversing Rust' and 'Old Retired Chal'
Makes no write/update/delete tool calls

evals.name: read-single-lookup
evals.prompt: In PocketBase, what's the single highest-point challenge in 'mcpskill_read'? Show me all of its field values.
evals.expected_output: find_records with sort="-points" and per_page=1 (or fetch_all then pick max). Identifies 'Buffer Overflow', points 500, difficulty hard, active true, and shows the id. No writes.
assertions: Identifies 'Buffer Overflow' as the highest-point row
Reports its points as 500 and difficulty as hard
Shows the record id
Does not fetch the whole collection with fetch_all unless it then correctly narrows to one row
Makes no write/update/delete tool calls

evals.name: list-schema-views
evals.prompt: Give me an inventory of every collection in our PocketBase, and tell me which ones are views rather than base or auth collections.
evals.expected_output: describe_schema(), then reports the collection list and names the 5 view collections: team_challenges_flags, _players_attempts, _team_players_stats, _dashboard_metrics, _submission_stats. Read-only.
assertions: Calls describe_schema
Answer names all 5 view collections: team_challenges_flags, _players_attempts, _team_players_stats, _dashboard_metrics, _submission_stats
Does not misclassify _superusers or admins as views (they are auth)
Makes no write/update/delete/schema-change tool calls

evals.name: create-collection-and-record
evals.prompt: In our PocketBase, create a new base collection called 'mcpskill_create' with these fields: title (text, required), body (text), pinned (bool). Then add one record: title 'hello', pinned true. Tell me the new record's id.
evals.expected_output: connect as superuser if needed, manage_collection(action="create", collection_type="base", fields=[...]) with the three field dicts, then write_record(action="create", data={"title":"hello","pinned":true}). Returns the created record id.
assertions: Creates collection 'mcpskill_create' via manage_collection with exactly the fields title (text, required), body (text), pinned (bool)
Creates one record with title 'hello' and pinned true
Reports the actual record id returned by the create call
After the run, collection mcpskill_create exists and contains exactly one record matching title='hello' and pinned=true

evals.name: update-record
evals.prompt: In the 'mcpskill_update' collection in PocketBase, find the challenge titled 'Alpha' and change its points to 500 and set active to false. Confirm what you changed.
evals.expected_output: find_records with filter_template="title = {:t}" to get Alpha's id, then write_record(action="update", record_id=..., data={"points":500,"active":false}). Confirms the id and the two changed fields.
assertions: Looks up the 'Alpha' record id via find_records before updating (does not guess the id)
Calls write_record with action="update" and the resolved record_id
Update data changes only points and active, not title or difficulty
After the run, the 'Alpha' row in mcpskill_update has points=500 and active=false
The other two rows (Bravo, Charlie) are unchanged

evals.name: delete-filtered-with-confirm
evals.prompt: Delete every inactive challenge (active = false) from the 'mcpskill_delete' collection in PocketBase. Be careful about it.
evals.expected_output: find_records(fetch_all=True, fields="id", filter on active = {:a} / false) to get the exact count (2), surfaces the matches, then delete_records with the same filter_template and confirm_count=2. Ends with 2 rows remaining (Keep One, Keep Two).
assertions: Counts the matching rows with find_records before deleting
Calls delete_records with confirm_count equal to the real match count (2)
Selects rows via filter_template + filter_params or via explicit record_ids, not by deleting the whole collection
After the run, mcpskill_delete contains exactly the 2 rows 'Keep One' and 'Keep Two'
Surfaces the matched rows or a count to the user before the delete call

evals.name: bulk-insert-atomic
evals.prompt: Add these 5 challenges to the 'mcpskill_bulk' collection in PocketBase, all in one atomic batch: 'Pwn 1' (100 pts, easy), 'Pwn 2' (200 pts, medium), 'Pwn 3' (300 pts, medium), 'Pwn 4' (400 pts, hard), 'Pwn 5' (500 pts, hard). All active.
evals.expected_output: A single bulk_write call with 5 create operations (not 5 separate write_record calls). After the run mcpskill_bulk holds all 5 rows with the right points and difficulty.
assertions: Uses one bulk_write call for all 5 inserts rather than 5 individual write_record calls
All 5 operations are action="create" against collection mcpskill_bulk
After the run mcpskill_bulk contains exactly 5 rows with titles Pwn 1..Pwn 5 and matching points 100/200/300/400/500
Each row has active=true and the stated difficulty

evals.name: bulk-mixed-ops
evals.prompt: In the 'mcpskill_bulkmix' PocketBase collection, do this as one atomic operation: create two rows ('Batch A' 20 pts, 'Batch B' 30 pts, both easy and active) and update the existing 'Seed One' row to 99 points.
evals.expected_output: One bulk_write whose operations list mixes 2 creates and 1 update. The update op resolves 'Seed One' id first (via find_records). After the run: 3 rows total, Seed One at 99 pts, Batch A at 20, Batch B at 30.
assertions: Resolves the 'Seed One' record id with find_records before building the batch
Uses a single bulk_write call whose operations include 2 creates and 1 update
After the run mcpskill_bulkmix has exactly 3 rows
'Seed One' has points=99 after the run; 'Batch A' has 20 and 'Batch B' has 30
